A warm welcome to
We are an Ofsted rated Good Islamic Independent School Catering for children in the Early and Primary years
Learn about our approach to daily outdoor education.
Learn more about our unique Creative curriculum which infuses Halaqah, Arabic, Qur'aan and academic education.
Our Gallery contains images of our hands on approach to learning.
Click here to see our latest news and keep with all the events at our school.
headteachers welcome
I would like to begin by extending a very warm welcome to our prospective parents and guardians, children and visitors.
Unique Academy is an Independent Islamic school which provides a calm, purposeful and safe Islamic environment for children from the age of 2 through to 11 years old.
Our school was born out of a clear vision to provide young children with a holistic education which serves the core purpose of nourishing their fitrah (natural disposition), taqwa (God consciousness) and Eemaan (faith) in line with the statement of our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, which mentions,
“Every child is born upon the fitrah….” (Saheeh Bukhari, 1292)
We emphasise on nourishing the fitrah, as we understand the relationship between the spiritual, inner developmental psychology of each unique child and the impact that this can have on their mental well being and thus outward character and behaviour. This is also recognised in another hadeeth of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, which mentions,
“Verily, in the body is a piece of flesh which, if it is good, the entire body is good…truly, it is the heart. (Saheeh Bukhari, 52)
In light of this, we have developed a broad and balanced creative curriculum, which amalgamates Islamic education subject disciplines (Qur’aan, Arabic and Halaqah) and academic subject disciplines, in the form of 7 areas of learning in the early years and 12 National Curriculum subjects in Key Stage 1and 2, which are designed and delivered in a manner which fosters the holistic (all round/inner and outer) development of each child’s knowledge, skills and understanding as they progress through each year group.
The indoor activities and outdoor Forest School learning experiences as well as the wider concepts, skills set, universal values, principles and morals that we nourish , will help to develop children’s resilience as they embark on their learning journey and navigate life’s tests, striving to succeed, not only in this life also in the Hereafter, God Willing.
Unique Academy is a school where each unique child is valued and supported to learn, explore and achieve in order to reach their individual potential.
You are welcome to contact us if you would like to visit the school, meet our fantastic team, get to know more about our unique education and take a glimpse at the Islamic environment that we provide for our pupils.
We look forward to meeting you!
Mrs Hawwa Mbombo BA (Hons), MA, NPQH
Chair of Trustees and Founding Headteacher

Testimonials
Alhamdulillah, we are truly blessed to have our child attend Unique Academy, where the pursuit of knowledge is harmoniously blended with strong Islamic values. We appreciate the efforts taken by each teacher not only to instill in our children the teachings of the Quran and the Sunnah of our beloved Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) but also to promote a healthy and active lifestyle. The inclusion of physical activities in the curriculum not only benefits their physical health but also nurtures their social skills and teamwork.
" Dear Amina, It is with great pleasure that we accept this place for my son. I would like to take this opportunity to thank sister Hawwa and all you lovely sisters for making us feel very welcome and taking the time to meet me and my family. May Allah reward all of you for what you have accomplished and make this school a successful establishment for the future of our children. Jazakumullaahu khairan."
"I have seen a massive improvement in my child’s learning progress. She has learnt different duas along her academic journey. She is implementing the duas in her daily life. Unique Academy have been a great help."
We have also begun a fruitful partnership with Tiffin Girls Grammar School. This partnership entails a joint effort between Unique Academy and Tiffin Girls to strive for excellence.

pageCache.text:
our ethos, vison, mission and values
Our vision
To nurture the fitrah of every child through faith, character, and compassion.
Our Ethos
Unique Academy is founded upon an Islamic ethos. Our ultimate goal is to provide excellency in Islamic and academic education, enabling each unique child to develop holistically, into an upright British citizen who contributes positively to their community and to society. We aspire to put these positive values and behaviours into practice as part of our Deen (Islamic way of life).
Our mission statement
Our mission is to nurture confident, compassionate, and knowledgeable children within a safe and inspiring Islamic environment. We are dedicated to providing high-quality teaching for all children, recognising each as a unique creation of The Creator. Through engaging, challenging and holistic learning experiences, we aim to cultivate a lifelong love for seeking knowledge, laying firm foundations for success in this life and high aspirations for the Hereafter. We strive to prepare our children to live with respect, consideration, and tolerance, contributing positively to our diverse and multicultural British society.
Our Universally shared values (perks - t)
Use your time wisely and always try your best
Aim high and be proud of doing things really well
Be kind and treat others the way you want to be treated
Keep learning and asking questions
Be honest and true in what you say and do
Always be clear and truthful — no secrets or confusion
British values
Our aim is to create a caring, warm, Islamic atmosphere within which pupils can develop to their full potential. Through the teaching and practice of Islam, in the light of the Quran and Sunnah, we aim to help our children to develop a love for Allaah and to develop confidence in their identity as Muslim children who will become well-rounded British citizens.
At Unique Academy we uphold and teach pupils about British Values through SMSC. This enables us to ensure our children have an appreciation and understanding of the following values:
Democracy
Rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect
Tolerance
Democracy
The children have an opportunity to have their voices heard through our school Shura council, class ambassadors, eco committee and pupil surveys. The annual elections of both School Councillors and Eco Warriors are based on pupil votes.
Rule of Law
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. We actively encourage visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service to help reinforce this message.
Islaamic life is governed by the Quran and the Sunnah (the life of the Prophet Muhammad PBUH). We emphasise the importance of following the rules of the Islamic religion so that our children can live spiritually enriched lives.
Individual Liberty
At Unique Academy, the children are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school, we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make choices safely, through the provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our learning about E-Safety and during PSHE lessons. Whether it be through their choice in the level of challenge in their work, or their participation in our extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
Mutual Respect
Part of our Islamic ethos has revolved around creating a caring and respectful community where children, parents and staff feel welcome, safe and valued as individuals. The children are taught that respect particularly to visitors, adults working within our school and beyond, as well as towards their peers is important. Respect is promoted through assemblies, class ambassadors and our PSHEC curriculum.
Tolerance
The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) taught that living harmoniously meant helping one another, not being angry or envious of others and being good to our neighbours whatever their faith. This is achieved through our Islamic ethos and by enhancing pupils understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society. Assemblies and discussions are supported by learning in PSHE, RE or when learning about other cultures through History or Geography. At Unique Academy, we teach about all other faiths including Christianity, Judaism, Sikhism, Buddhism and Hinduism as part of our RE curriculum.
Our Upper Key Stage 2 class visited a Synagogue and we have invited visitors from Hope Church in the past to conduct our whole school assembly.

About Us
Unique Academy is part of Unique Knowledge Seekers Academy (UKSA) which is a UK registered educational charity. UKSA has been supporting children, young people and adults in the local community and beyond through its supplementary school service, UMTA, for nearly 5 years.
Unique Academy is focused on catering for children’s holistic development within the school’s Islamic ethos, unique vision, mission, values, curriculum and learning opportunities – all geared towards developing the fitrah.
Our school team consists of professionals with extensive background knowledge and experience in education, giving them the confidence to deliver a full-time school provision for the benefit of the local community and beyond.

Safeguarding - Sports Club
What parents should look for when choosing a sports club
Many parents encourage their children to take part in extra-curricular activities such as sports clubs or skill-based groups like football or martial arts, or even consider hiring a personal coach. These experiences can be incredibly positive—supporting a child’s development, boosting their self-esteem, and offering opportunities for fun and social interaction.
However, when selecting any club or activity, it’s vital for parents to feel confident that the environment is safe, supportive, and well-managed. A good sports club should not only nurture a child’s abilities but also prioritise their wellbeing and happiness.
Choosing the right group activity or club
If your child is interested in joining a group activity, such as learning a new sport or becoming part of a team, it’s important to visit the group beforehand to observe how it operates. Ideally, attend a typical session rather than a trial or showcase event. This allows you to see the group in its usual environment and get a feel for how the staff interact with the children and how the children respond.
Coaches and instructors may use different styles, some may be firm to maintain discipline, while others may be energetic and enthusiastic to motivate performance. It’s normal for children to feel a little nervous about new challenges, but they should never be visibly distressed or afraid of the coach or the activity.
Whether they are paid staff or volunteers, all coaches and instructors should behave in a professional and respectful manner, much like school staff. Working with children is a significant responsibility, and it is essential that those in these roles are well-trained, appropriately supported, and have the necessary skills and experience to work safely and positively with young people.
if your child tells you something inappropriate has happened
It is vital to listen carefully to your child and take seriously anything they disclose. Reassure them that they have done the right thing by speaking up, and make it clear that they are not to blame.
If you are concerned that a coach or tutor has displayed poor practice—meaning their actions were inappropriate or unprofessional, though not necessarily abusive or criminal—it is advisable to stop your child’s participation in the activity until you’ve had the opportunity to seek further guidance.
If you are concerned that a coach or tutor may have:
you should contact the Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO) for advice and support: Email: lado@hounslow.gov.uk | Grace.Murphy@hounslow.gov.uk Telephone: 0208 583 5730 | 0208 583 4933 |07975 820 130
If you believe a crime has been committed, contact the Police immediately.
Quick checklist for parents
Before enrolling your child in a sports club or activity group, use this checklist to ensure they will be safe, supported, and well cared for:
Safeguarding & Welfare
Policies & Procedures
Are there safe recruitment practices in place, including:
A well-managed club will welcome your interest and be happy to share information about their safeguarding practices. They understand the trust you place in them when you leave your child in their care.
Role descriptions
Reference checks
Enhanced DBS checks for relevant positions
Appropriate qualifications for coaches and staff

Curriculum meeting information
Curriculum
Here at Unique Academy we provide a knowledge rich, broad, balanced and coherent creative curriculum using themes from Cornerstones Curriculum Maestro, which is designed to deliver outstanding learning experiences for children.
What is the Cornerstones Curriculum? The Cornerstones Curriculum is a creative and thematic approach to learning that is mapped to the 2014 primary National Curriculum to ensure comprehensive coverage of national expectations. It is based on a child-centred pedagogy and at Unique Academy, we base our teaching and learning experiences on our Islamic ethos as well as Knowledge Rich Projects (KRPs) from Cornerstones, which combined provide a rich menu of exciting and motivating learning activities that make creative links between all aspects of children’s learning and our Islamic values. We believe children learn better when they are encouraged to use their imagination and apply their learning to engaging contexts. Our curriculum provides many learning challenges throughout the academic year that require children to solve problems, apply themselves creatively and express their knowledge and understanding effectively. The curriculum also provides rigorous skills and knowledge framework that outlines the end of year expectations in all subjects. These skills and knowledge are tied to activities and are age-related so that staff can track children’s progress on a daily basis and identify their individual learning needs.
Reading At The Heart Of The Curriculum
At Unique Academy, the children will learn how to read using the fun and interactive synthetics phonics programme Jolly Phonics. More information about this programme can be found in this link: https://www.jollylearning.co.uk/jolly-phonics/
The children will also experience a wide range of reading opportunities through:
Encouraging daily reading
Celebrate reading through special events

We want to ensure that our provision matches the learning and development needs of all of our children. As we have a large amount of children in our setting whom English is not the dominant language at home, we ensure our setting is equitable and inclusive for all our children.
We work with parents as partners.
SEND
Learn English at home (LEAH)
LEAH supports adults in learning English, particularly those who may face barriers to accessing traditional adult education classes. Their lessons are designed to help individuals communicate their basic and everyday needs in English. This service is especially suitable for those who:
Have physical or mental health challenges.
